Title: gemini-api-key secret never provisioned in Terraform despite Gemini becoming the production-default model provider
Description:
Current behaviour: services/model-router/src/Api/appsettings.json now sets Router.Mode to "single-gemini" and ModelCatalog.SingleDefault to "gemini-3.1-pro" as the production defaults, with Gemini.ApiKeySecretName = "gemini-api-key". However "gemini" does not appear anywhere under deploy/modules/ or deploy/environments/ (verified via grep -rl -i "gemini" deploy/ — only matches under deploy/local/ and deploy/docker-compose.yml, i.e. the new local preview files, not the Terraform IaC). deploy/environments/dev/secrets.tf only defines model-router-foundry-api-key and model-router-anthropic-api-key as Key Vault secrets; there is no equivalent entry or Terraform variable for a Gemini API key.
Expected behaviour: Before Gemini can serve as the production-default LLM provider, a gemini-api-key Key Vault secret must exist and be wired through the same pattern as the existing Foundry/Anthropic secrets (a Terraform variable sourced from a GitHub secret, a secrets.tf entry, and any necessary container-apps/main.tf wiring).
Affected files: deploy/environments/dev/secrets.tf; deploy/modules/container-apps/main.tf; services/model-router/src/Api/appsettings.json:72-77 (Router.Mode, Gemini.ApiKeySecretName)
Impact: Even after Bug 1 (KeyResolver default) is fixed to use Key Vault correctly, Gemini calls will still fail in production because the gemini-api-key secret was never created in Key Vault. The production-default LLM provider has no working credential path end-to-end.
ReproSteps:
1. Fix KeyResolver:Provider to "KeyVault" (Bug 1 fix) and deploy model-router to Container Apps.
2. Call any model-router endpoint that routes to Gemini (the new default, Router:Mode=single-gemini).
3. KeyVaultProviderKeyResolver attempts to fetch secret "gemini-api-key" from the deployed Key Vault.
4. The secret does not exist because it was never added to deploy/environments/*/secrets.tf, so the fetch fails.
Discussion:
FINDING: gemini-api-key secret is never provisioned anywhere in Terraform, but Gemini is now the production-default primary provider. The root cause is that the router configuration was updated to use Gemini as the default (Router:Mode = single-gemini, ModelCatalog.SingleDefault = gemini-3.1-pro) but the supporting infrastructure (Key Vault secret, Terraform variables, and environment wiring) was never added to the IaC. This follows the existing pattern for Foundry and Anthropic keys in secrets.tf. Fix: Add a gemini-api-key Key Vault secret following the same Terraform pattern as model-router-foundry-api-key and model-router-anthropic-api-key (Terraform variable sourced from GitHub secret, secrets.tf entry, container-apps/main.tf wiring) before Gemini can serve as the prod-default provider.
RESOLUTION: Added var.gemini_api_key (deploy/environments/dev/variables.tf, sensitive, sourced via TF_VAR_gemini_api_key / GitHub secret GEMINI_API_KEY, same pattern as ai_resource_api_key) and a "gemini-api-key" entry in local.kv_secrets (deploy/environments/dev/secrets.tf), written through the existing azurerm_key_vault_secret.platform for_each — no container-apps/main.tf change needed since KeyVaultProviderKeyResolver fetches secrets by name dynamically at call time via the already-injected KeyVault:Uri, not via a per-secret env var. terraform validate unverified (terraform CLI not installed on this machine) — the change is a straight copy of the existing model-router-foundry-api-key pattern, low risk, but Alpha should run `terraform -chdir=deploy/environments/dev validate` before applying. prod/ environment intentionally left untouched — it's already missing the Foundry/Anthropic secrets too (pre-existing dev/prod drift, out of scope here).
